analysis.investment_thesis: Blue Dart is a quality logistics franchise but it is a large-cap MNC subsidiary (DHL owns 75%) with declining profitability — net profit fell from 382 Cr in FY22 to 252 Cr in FY25 — priced at 44x P/E with only 9.3% revenue CAGR over nine years. There is no SMILE here: no smallness, no transformation catalyst, and no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Premium brand in Indian express logistics with a strong network moat — 5/5 years of positive OCF (735 Cr in FY25) proves earnings quality
Promoter holding effectively 75% through DHL parent — capital return discipline visible (consistent financing outflows of 291-434 Cr/year)
E-commerce and B2B logistics tailwind provides a secular demand floor for premium express delivery
key_risks: Net profit in secular decline: 382 Cr (FY22) → 371 Cr (FY23) → 301 Cr (FY24) → 252 Cr (FY25) despite revenue growing from 4,410 to 5,720 Cr — cost structure is worsening
Structural competition from Delhivery, Ekart, Xpressbees, and Ecom Express is eroding pricing power at the premium end
Lease liabilities (borrowings ~1,081 Cr) inflate EV, constraining financial flexibility; EBITDA has contracted from 1,116 Cr to 894 Cr in last 5 years
red_flags: Market cap 12,792 Cr and P/E 44x on a business with 2.8% net profit CAGR over 9 years — no value at any reasonable growth assumption
MNC subsidiary structure: DHL sets strategic direction; Indian minority shareholders benefit last, not from a hungry Indian promoter vision
EBITDA trend explicitly contracting over last 5 years — operating leverage is negative, meaning this is a mature/declining business, not an expansion story
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Blue Dart is a business I respect but cannot buy. It is a mature, high-quality logistics franchise that has peaked in terms of margin expansion — EBITDA contracted from 1,116 Cr in FY21 to 894 Cr in FY25 despite revenue growing 74%. The business is now in a structural squeeze between rising aviation and lease costs and increasing price competition from tech-enabled startups.

More critically, the 'promoter' is DHL Singapore — a foreign MNC optimising for global logistics strategy, not an Indian promoter with a 10x vision for this market. The P/E of 44x for 2.8% net profit CAGR and declining absolute profits is a valuation that can only compress from here. Hard pass.
